core_obligations: Reduce to the case of a single quotient, set up the notation for the tail ideal, and rewrite the graded pieces of the quotient module (proof lines 17254-17262).

Reduce further to the identity J^{n+1}M + J^nM intersected with f_1 M equal to J^{n+1}M + f_1 J^{n-1}M, which exhibits the associated graded of the quotient as that of M modulo the variable X_1 (proof lines 17263-17270).
Verify that identity using that the associated graded module is the polynomial algebra by the quasi-regularity assumption (proof lines 17270-17273).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to one element and express the graded pieces of the quotient (proof lines 17253-17262).
Prove the intersection identity from the polynomial description of the associated graded (proof lines 17263-17274).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if f_1, ..., f_c is an M-quasi-regular sequence, then the tail f_{i+1}, ..., f_c is quasi-regular for M modulo the earlier elements (statement lines 17243-17251). The proof does not redo the definition: it reduces to the case of one element, rewrites the graded pieces of the quotient module as quotients of the graded pieces of M, and isolates the intersection identity J^n M intersected with f_1 M equal to f_1 J^{n-1}M, which it verifies from the assumption that the associated graded of M is a polynomial algebra (proof lines 17253-17274). Locating the crux in that single intersection is the content of the argument, and the author writes both reductions out. H2.
